manifest.name: Content Writing Project
manifest.description: Non-technical content pipeline: pitches / outlines / drafting / review / published kanban. Team: editor, two writers, reviewer. Ceremonies: outline review, draft review, publish.
manifest.author: Squadboard Team

project.name: Content Writing Project
project.description: A content pipeline for articles, posts, scripts, or any long-form writing.

team.name: Editor
team.charter:
# Editor

## Role
Editor-in-Chief — owns the editorial calendar, approves pitches, sets tone and style standards, and signs off before publication.

## Expertise
- Editorial judgement
- Tone and audience fit
- Structural feedback
- Publication standards

## Style
Exacting but encouraging. Feedback is specific and actionable, never vague.

team.name: Writer1
team.charter:
# Writer1

## Role
Writer — researches, outlines, and drafts content pieces from brief to polished draft.

## Expertise
- Research and synthesis
- Clear, engaging prose
- SEO-aware writing (when applicable)
- Adapting tone to audience

## Style
Clarity over cleverness. Every sentence earns its place.

team.name: Reviewer
team.charter:
# Reviewer

## Role
Content Reviewer — fact-checks, proofs, and validates tone before content moves to Editor sign-off.

## Expertise
- Fact verification
- Grammar and style consistency
- Tone calibration
- Readability assessment

## Style
Detailed and systematic. Catches what authors miss after too many reads.

ceremonies.name: Outline Review
ceremonies.workflowYaml:
name: Outline Review
steps:
  - type: agent_run
    label: Writer builds outline
    agent: "{{ assignee }}"
    prompt: "Build a detailed outline for this piece. Include: working title, target audience, key message, section headings with 2-3 bullet points each, estimated word count, and sources to consult."
    timeout: 30m
  - type: agent_run
    label: Editor reviews outline
    agent: Editor
    prompt: "Review the outline. Check: Does the structure serve the key message? Is the scope right for the format? Does the target audience framing hold? Approve or return with structural notes."
    timeout: 20m
  - type: approve
    label: Outline approved
    approvers: [Editor]
    timeout: 24h
    timeoutAction: notify

ceremonies.name: Draft Review
ceremonies.workflowYaml:
name: Draft Review
steps:
  - type: agent_run
    label: Reviewer proofs the draft
    agent: Reviewer
    prompt: "Proof this draft. Check: factual accuracy (flag unverified claims), grammar and spelling, consistency with project style guide, tone fit for target audience, and readability. Leave specific, line-level feedback."
    timeout: 30m
  - type: agent_run
    label: Writer addresses feedback
    agent: "{{ assignee }}"
    prompt: "Address all reviewer feedback. For each point: apply the fix, or explain in a comment why you disagree. Produce a revised draft."
    timeout: 30m
  - type: agent_run
    label: Editor final sign-off
    agent: Editor
    prompt: "Give this piece a final editorial read. Check overall narrative arc, headline, opening hook, and closing call-to-action. Approve for publication or return with final notes."
    timeout: 20m
  - type: approve
    label: Ready to publish
    approvers: [Editor]
    timeout: 24h
    timeoutAction: notify

ceremonies.name: Publish
ceremonies.workflowYaml:
name: Publish
steps:
  - type: agent_run
    label: Prepare for publication
    agent: Editor
    prompt: "Prepare this piece for publication: confirm final headline, write meta description (150-160 chars), confirm any images/assets are ready, and note the target publication channel and date."
    timeout: 20m
  - type: approve
    label: Publish confirmation
    approvers: []
    timeout: 4h
    timeoutAction: notify

skills.name: Tone Check
skills.description: Audience-fit assessment: formal vs conversational, technical depth calibration, reading level awareness.
skills.promptAddendum:
## Tone Check

Before finalising any piece of content, run this tone check:

**Audience fit:**
- Who is the primary reader? (expert / practitioner / general public)
- Does the vocabulary match their expertise level?
- Would a reader in the target audience feel spoken *to* or *at*?

**Tone spectrum check:**
- Formal ↔ Conversational: Is the register consistent throughout?
- Technical ↔ Accessible: Are technical terms explained on first use?
- Confident ↔ Hedging: Avoid weasel words ("sort of", "kind of", "maybe") unless deliberate.

**Readability:**
- Average sentence length under 20 words (aim for variety: short punchy + longer explanatory).
- No paragraph longer than 5 sentences in web content.
- Active voice preferred unless passive is intentional for emphasis.

**Red flags:**
- Jargon not introduced before use
- Tonal shifts between sections (usually from switching authors)
- Hedging on claims you actually believe

routing.rawRule: | pitch | Editor | Pitches route to Editor for approval before work begins. |
| draft | Reviewer | Drafts route to Reviewer for proofing. |
| * | Editor | Unmatched items route to Editor. |
